sample_unit: ED encounters meeting inclusion criteria (children with suspected sepsis)
models_evaluated: machine-learning septic shock prediction models (at arrival and 2 hours)

links.outcome: Antibiotic and bolus within 1 hour; hypotensive shock; time-to-antibiotic in stepped-wedge cluster RCT of predictive CDS
links.effect: Antibiotic and bolus within 1 hour: 39.0% intervention vs 38.9% control (aOR 1.07 [0.61-1.88]); shock aOR 1.12 (0.53-2.46); antibiotic timeliness aHR 0.85 (0.63-1.16). No difference.
links.quote: Antibiotic and bolus within 1 hour occurred in 39.0% of patients in the intervention arm versus 38.9% of patients in the control arm (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 1.07 [0.61-1.88]).

screen.reason: This stepped-wedge cluster randomized trial evaluated the deployment of a machine learning-based clinical decision support tool for pediatric septic shock in real emergency department workflows.
